_readme: Structured log of what's built and what's backlog, each with the trade-off behind it. Written in the same style used to scope work for a coding agent in slices — see CLAUDE.md for the conventions this follows.

shipped.summary: Chat with GPT-5.4 Mini, GPT-5.3 Codex, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and DeepSeek V3.2 through one streaming UI.
shipped.rationale: Each provider has a different request/response shape (Chat Completions, Responses API, Anthropic Messages). A declarative model registry (src/lib/models.ts) isolates that difference so the UI and the chat route stay provider-agnostic.
shipped.tradeoff: No provider-specific features (prompt caching, extended thinking, parallel tool calls) exposed yet — lowest-common-denominator streaming contract.

shipped.summary: Attach a PDF/Word file to chat; its content stays in context across a long conversation.
shipped.rationale: History is trimmed by message count to control token cost, but a naively trimmed document reference silently disappears mid-conversation.
shipped.tradeoff: Pinning + trimming must filter the original array in place to preserve user/assistant alternation — concatenating pinned + recent breaks it and the Anthropic API rejects the result.

shipped.summary: Turn the conversation into a branded .pptx deck.
shipped.rationale: The model writes a pptxgenjs script directly rather than filling a fixed template, so slide structure can vary with the conversation, not just the text in fixed boxes.
shipped.tradeoff: Code-gen is less reliable than structured output into a template. Mitigated with a syntax check, a truncate-to-last-good-line recovery pass, one automatic retry, and execFile (no shell) for execution safety.

shipped.summary: Dollar-based monthly spend tracker per model, shown in the sidebar.
shipped.rationale: Zero backend state needed for an MVP on a small, trusted shared budget.
shipped.tradeoff: Explicitly a usage nudge, not a spend cap — resettable via browser storage. A real ceiling needs server-side enforcement; see backlog.

shipped.summary: Azure Entra ID sign-in via App Service Easy Auth.
shipped.rationale: Easy Auth injects a trusted principal header after OIDC sign-in — no session/token-handling code of our own to get wrong.
shipped.tradeoff: Platform lock-in to Azure App Service. Bypassed outside production (Easy Auth's endpoints don't exist under `next dev`) so the repo runs and is reviewable without a live Azure tenant.

shipped.summary: This repo itself: a focused, anonymized, chat-only extract of a larger internal tool (which also has a RAG knowledge-search pipeline and a multi-step proposal-document generator).
shipped.rationale: A clean rewrite of the UI layer (rather than stripping the original down) kept the extracted app small and fully legible, instead of carrying dead state through from the multi-tab original.
shipped.tradeoff: Rewrite cost more upfront than deletion would have, in exchange for a result with no leftover surface area from the removed features.

backlog.summary: A real budget ceiling behind the current client-side nudge.
backlog.rationale: Needed the moment this has to hold against a user trying to get around it, not just a shared-budget nudge for trusted users.

backlog.summary: Expose prompt caching and extended thinking for Claude, parallel tool calls for GPT, instead of the current lowest-common-denominator streaming contract.
backlog.rationale: Current routing abstraction trades these away for a uniform UI contract; worth revisiting for an agentic (not just chat) use case.

backlog.summary: Catch and repair runtime failures in generated pptxgenjs scripts, not just syntax errors.
backlog.rationale: `node --check` only catches syntax errors — a correctly-formed call to the wrong pptxgenjs method still throws mid-render today.
Client-side-only quota can't answer 'which model do people actually reach for' — the obvious next question once this is in real use.
